questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I found the connection between Denmark and France interesting and got the opertunity to experience Paris. The CY Cergy Paris university promoted themselves as a University with professors and educators with experience from a Paris private law aspect. Furthermore was i able to take all courses in english, which was the biggest factor in my choice.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is fun but demanding.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was descent. I got emails informing me on when and where to meet.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received at powerpoint with information, that i found very helpful during the semester.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I applied for Fondation Danoise in CIUP. By contacting Campus France in Denmark it was easy to apply there.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That you should expect an expensive rent, but that it's worth it. Cergy is not worth living in and most other exchange students i met in CY Cergy Paris university agreed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The administration was unable to communicate in person in englsih. Not good for a university offering so many courses in english, since exchange students pick their university mostly based on being unable to speak french. This gave me a bad experience in changing courses since i had to show up at the office and point to the computer which courses i wished to change and i couldn't get my questions answered. 
They were good at responding in email, however sometimes it is easier to understand in person, why the process became longer than neccesary.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Easy. Most of the work was done from home in good time.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Powerpoint slides from intro day had alot of info with phonenumbers, who had which responsibility (who to call if you needed to change courses), difference between CM and TD courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: One of my classes overlapped with another why i had to change, but otherwise i got the classes i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Arm yourself with patience. They are unable to speak english in person, but are happy to help when you send email. It just takes time. Furthermore be well prepared from home.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: BA courses were way below the level in Denmark. This can be because of the english level in France. However the LL.M. classes were fine, why i think CY Cergy Paris University should consider offering more than just 2 LL.M classes to Danish students and 3 to UK/US students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Little to nothing to read for every class but intense teaching while students take notes. Some classes were literally hours of the teacher reading up from a screen and students taking notes. 

Very different from Denmark which has no participation grade and alot of reading done from home to prepare for class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
UK Business law I
Argumentation and Negotiation I
Moot court and litigation
LL.M. Tort law
LL.M. Intro to french and civil law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do the same courses as i did. Argumentation and Negotiation is chill, same with Business law where you are not obligated to show up for class and can read from home. LL.M. courses are on a level that actually can challenge you a little. Chose intro to french law and civil law, because it's interesting to learn about the system in the country you are on echange in. Same with tort law which has a good professor and interesting to compare tort law in Denmark and France.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing. Good tip is to prepare that everything is expensive and nightlife in Paris costs alot.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Foods, like eggs, milk and cheese was cheaper than in Denmark. Furthermore eating out was less expensive than i initially expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were some oppertunities with sport, but it wasn't so easy to attend and they didn't promote it so well. ELSA were good at having events.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Handball, combatsports, Moot court competition, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ELSA had many events

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Experience Paris and outside of Paris. Café, boulangerie, restaurants, events (Fashion week and european cultural heritage days). Furthermore experience champagne east of Paris and Normandy west of Paris.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy in some ways. People in Paris are kind of rude especially in public transport. However many other people are helpful. It's a large city and you can feel that, but it doesn't take long until you adjust.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Do some sports or go do activities in Paris like seeing museums, nightlife, etc.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Food, art and experiences. The vibe of Paris is that it's a city filled with different types of people which makes it very diverse and accepting. Furthermore it's so picturesque.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Do not go there for an academic challenge. Go there if you wish to experience Paris and for gods sake do not live in Cergy, but find a place in Paris. Paris is worth the commute.
2. Be prepared for all the typical things (Where to live, transport to study, courses, economy) before you go so you can enjoy Paris
3. Take the french courses (they are free offered by the university)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for a room at Fondation Danoise. Any house in the CIUP is nice since you get to live in a dorm and automaticly meet other students who also are on exchange.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends and experiences like normandy trip with friends from study, and motorcycle trip east of Paris to champagne and Ardennes. It's also a good location to get visits from friends. i experienced that many friends wanted to come visit and see Paris.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Speaking french. I evolved from being a person with no experience in french to ordering at restaurants and having simple conversations in french. Studying in english is furthermore a challenge itself which was cool to master.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
